trigger: a replay-ADOPTED session's reannounce-triggered CONNECTED notify is dropped at ?MAX_NOTIFY_INFLIGHT capacity or during a circuit-open window (a fleet-wide reconnect storm is the named, realistic trigger)
summary: SUPERSEDES: BatchHeartbeat's renew_leases unconditionally extended lease_until on every heartbeat regardless of whether cluster_id had ever converged, so a row stuck with cluster_id=NULL after a dropped reannounce stayed 'alive' (agent heartbeating normally) but permanently non-routable forever, with nothing ever re-tombstoning it for a later reclaim attempt (I6 raised to HIGH via clause (a) false assurance -- the ADR's own 'Fixed'/'CLOSED' framing of the reannounce mechanism did not disclose this). FIXED: renew_leases's SET clause is now a CASE that leaves lease_until untouched when cluster_id IS NULL, so an unconverged row reaches its own ordinary TTL+grace expiry and is tombstoned by the existing, unmodified reap_stale_routes() sweep, giving the next replay (or the agent's own reconnect) another reclaim attempt. A converged row is unaffected (announce_connected always grants a full fresh lease on every genuine CONNECTED). Two new regression tests added: 'renew_leases does NOT extend the lease for a row still lacking a converged cluster_id' and the four pre-existing BatchHeartbeat/re-announce tests updated to call announce_connected first so their lease-renewal assertions remain meaningful under the new semantics.
